messages.subject: CRS of inla.mesh.2d
parts:
I have constructed a mesh using the inla.mesh.2d function.
The inputs are in the same CRS, and the mesh seems to be made and plots nicely, with the following code:
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(boundary = CNP,                     
loc=st_coordinates(final2),               
      max.edge = c(1,2)*max.edge,   
                  offset=c(max.edge, bound.outer),   
                  cutoff = max.edge/5, 
                    crs = crs(final2))

However, when I fit the lgcp model, I get this error:
> fit <- lgcp(  
components = cmp, 
data = nests_,
samplers = transects,  
domain = list(    
coordinates = mesh,    
distance = INLA::inla.mesh.1d(seq(0, W, length.out = 30))
   ),
   formula = form,
   options = list(bru_initial = list(lsig = 2),
                  bru_verbose=4)
 )
iinla: Evaluate component inputs
Error in st_geos_binop("intersects", x, y, sparse = sparse, prepared = prepared,  :   st_crs(x) == st_crs(y) is not TRUE


It seems that the mesh crs and crs of inputs don't match - is this likely the issue?
> st_crs(CNP) == st_crs(final2)
[1] TRUE
> st_crs(mesh) == st_crs(final2)
[1] FALSE

What would be the fix for this? I've tried to transform the Mesh CRS but doesn't seem to be working.
Thanks!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] CRS of inla.mesh.2d
parts:
Hi,

1. The mesh CRS info still needs to be given as an sp CRS, e.g. use crs=fm_CRS(final2)
2. What INLA and inlabru versions do you have. Make sure you have at least the latest CRAN version of inlabru, 2.8.0 (which now handles most of the CRS related geometry operations in inla).
3. After fixing step 1 above, compare the contents of fm_crs() for each of the three objects.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: CRS of inla.mesh.2d
parts:
You need fm_crs(mesh) to extract an sf CRS for the mesh, not st_crs.
Also, look at the actual crs output. Sometimes the difference is a difference in the “input” part, which shouldn’t matter. fm_crs() and fm_CRS() attempt to produce consistent output.

Finn

Check
print(bru_safe_inla())

Finn

I've made the following changes to my code but still get inconsistent CRS when fitting LGCP and the same error message.

> crs = fm_CRS(final2)
> mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(boundary = CNP,
                      loc=st_coordinates(final2),
                     max.edge = c(1,2)*max.edge,
                      offset=c(max.edge, bound.outer),
                      cutoff = max.edge/5,
                      crs = crs)

> st_crs(mesh)
Coordinate Reference System: NA
> st_crs(CNP) == st_crs(final2)
[1] TRUE
> st_crs(mesh) == st_crs(final2)
[1] FALSE
> st_crs(mesh) == st_crs(CNP)
[1] FALSE> View(crs)
On Wednesday, July 5, 2023 at 12:23:35 PM UTC+1 Lucy Clarke wrote:
I have constructed a mesh using the inla.mesh.2d function.
The inputs are in the same CRS, and the mesh seems to be made and plots nicely, with the following code:
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(boundary = CNP,                     
loc=st_coordinates(final2),               
      max.edge = c(1,2)*max.edge,   
                  offset=c(max.edge, bound.outer),   
                  cutoff = max.edge/5, 
                    crs = crs(final2))

However, when I fit the lgcp model, I get this error:
> fit <- lgcp(  
components = cmp, 
data = nests_,
samplers = transects,  
domain = list(    
coordinates = mesh,    
distance = INLA::inla.mesh.1d(seq(0, W, length.out = 30))
   ),
   formula = form,
   options = list(bru_initial = list(lsig = 2),
                  bru_verbose=4)
 )
iinla: Evaluate component inputs
Error in st_geos_binop("intersects", x, y, sparse = sparse, prepared = prepared,  :   st_crs(x) == st_crs(y) is not TRUE


It seems that the mesh crs and crs of inputs don't match - is this likely the issue?
> st_crs(CNP) == st_crs(final2)
[1] TRUE
> st_crs(mesh) == st_crs(final2)
[1] FALSE

What would be the fix for this? I've tried to transform the Mesh CRS but doesn't seem to be working.
Thanks!

Sorry, I meant
print(bru_safe_sp())

Finn

On 5 Jul 2023, at 13:57, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿You may also need to upgrade to the latest inla version, in case the problem is in there; the latest version relies on inlabru for the geometry handling, making it a bit more up-to-date.  Also check that you have the latest sp version, as there are known issues with the previous ones with default settings.

Check
print(bru_safe_inla())

Finn

On 5 Jul 2023, at 13:54, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿One of the articles on https://inlabru-org.github.io/inlabru/index.html has (experimentally, as the data set naming might change) been converted from sp to sf, showing the basics; the basic lgcp example in two dimensions. The menu links to both the sp and sf versions.

Finn

On 5 Jul 2023, at 13:28, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Hard to tell without seeing the entire model definition.
You should be using either all sp objects or sf objects, and not mix the two. (When given a mix, I tries it’s best, but it’s not well defined)

Finn

On 5 Jul 2023, at 13:16, Lucy Clarke <lvcla...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿
Thanks, my mistake - using fm_crs(mesh) == st_crs(final2) now comes out as true.

Looking at the crs ouputs for the mesh - it's a list of 2 and the input crs looks correct and to match final2 data. Is there a reason that I still cannot fit the lgcp and I'm still getting this error? Do I need to amend the wkt crs? Plotting the mesh alone plots it in lon/lat which I am surprised by? Sorry if I am missing something obvious here!

Thanks!

On Wednesday, July 5, 2023 at 12:52:38 PM UTC+1 Finn Lindgren wrote:
You need fm_crs(mesh) to extract an sf CRS for the mesh, not st_crs.
Also, look at the actual crs output. Sometimes the difference is a difference in the “input” part, which shouldn’t matter. fm_crs() and fm_CRS() attempt to produce consistent output.

Finn
